Tesla Cybercab orders open at $29,990 + $299/mo, only in Robotaxi zones

EV
By Dr. Ethan Vance Chief EV & Battery Systems Fellow • via Electrek Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Electrek Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights
  • Tesla is now inviting “select customers” to buy a Cybercab for personal use at $29,990, but the car won’t move unless you also pay $299 a month for an “Autonomy Subscription.” And it only works inside Tesla’s Robotaxi service areas in Texas and Florida, the same geofences that have turned out to be significantly smaller than what Tesla advertises.
  • Tesla is now inviting “select customers” to buy a Cybercab for personal use at $29,990, but the car won’t move unless you also pay $299 a month for an “Autonomy Subscription.”.
  • And it only works inside Tesla’s Robotaxi service areas in Texas and Florida, the same geofences that have turned out to be significantly smaller than what Tesla advertises.
  • Tesla’s official Robotaxi account announced the invites on X on Friday with screenshots of the order page and the invitation email.
⚡ EDITORIAL TAKE • DR. ETHAN VANCE Chief EV & Battery Systems Fellow

The Electrification & Charging Infrastructure Horizon

Beyond the immediate headline, this development marks a critical inflection point in the broader EV transition. As automakers and charging networks race to lower consumer friction, the reporting from Electrek highlights that battery energy density, thermal management, and raw cost per kilowatt-hour remain the ultimate battlegrounds. For prospective EV buyers and fleet operators, tracking these operational metrics offers clear guidance on vehicle longevity and residual value.

Big Picture: Global battery production scale and grid upgrades will define whether mass-market adoption targets are met over the next 24 months.

Tesla is now inviting “select customers” to buy a Cybercab for personal use at $29,990, but the car won’t move unless you also pay $299 a month for an “Autonomy Subscription.”

📌 The Core Development

And it only works inside Tesla’s Robotaxi service areas in Texas and Florida, the same geofences that have turned out to be significantly smaller than what Tesla advertises.

Tesla’s official Robotaxi account announced the invites on X on Friday with screenshots of the order page and the invitation email.

🔍 Background & Sector Context

The order page lists the Cybercab at $29,990 before taxes, with an estimated delivery of December 2026 in Austin, Texas. You need to put down a $1,000 non-refundable deposit to order.

The subscription isn’t optional. It’s pre-checked on the order page at $299 per month, with one month included, and the fine print says “Subscription and regular vehicle maintenance required to operate.”

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

The rest is what we already knew. Two seats, a 21-inch center touchscreen, 20.1 cubic feet of cargo space, and no steering wheel or pedals. Tesla calls it “fully autonomous” and says you’ll “manage your ride in the app.”

Musk had promised a Cybercab “below $30,000” when he unveiled it in 2024. He technically hit it. He just didn’t mention the $3,588 a year it takes to use it. Over five years, that’s about $47,600 for a two-seater, before insurance, maintenance, taxes, and charging.
